record.paper_title: AUTOMORPHISMS AND DYNAMICS: A LIST OF OPEN PROBLEMS
record.context_brief: Invariant nef classes and fibrations on Calabi–Yau threefolds
record.original_question: Let X be a Calabi–Yau threefold and let f be an automorphism of X whose action on cohomology is non-trivial and unipotent. If κ is a Kähler form on X with cohomology class [κ] ∈ H^2(X; R), then n^{-k}(f^n)^*[κ] converges to an f-invariant nef class. Is this limiting f-invariant nef class induced by, or otherwise directly related to, an f-invariant fibration on X?

evidence.quote: So, let f be an automorphism of a Calabi-Yau variety X of dimension 3, with a non-trivial unipotent action on the cohomology. Consider a kähler form κ on X, with cohomology class [κ] ∈ H2(X; R); then n−k(f n)∗[κ] converges towards an f-invariant nef class. Is this class related to an f-invariant fibration on X ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth Calabi–Yau threefold over $\mathbb{C}$ (a smooth projective threefold with trivial canonical bundle and $h^{1}(\mathcal{O}_X)=0$). Let $f\colon X\to X$ be an automorphism, and assume that the induced linear action $f^{*}$ on $H^{*}(X;\mathbb{R})$ is non-trivial and unipotent (i.e. $f^{*}-\mathrm{Id}$ is nilpotent but $f^{*}\neq\mathrm{Id}$). Let $\kappa$ be a Kähler form on $X$ with cohomology class $[\kappa]\in H^{2}(X;\mathbb{R})$, and let $k$ be the largest integer such that $(f^{*}-\mathrm{Id})^{k}[\kappa]\neq 0$ on $H^{2}(X;\mathbb{R})$. Then the sequence $n^{-k}(f^{n})^{*}[\kappa]$ converges in $H^{2}(X;\mathbb{R})$ to a non-zero $f^{*}$-invariant nef class $\alpha$.

Question: Is this limit class $\alpha$ induced by (or otherwise canonically associated with) an $f$-invariant fibration $X\to Y$ onto a lower-dimensional normal variety $Y$ — for instance, by being the pullback of an ample (or nef and big) class from $Y$?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface related work on fibered Calabi–Yau threefolds with positive-entropy automorphisms preserving a fibration, and on the cone conjecture, but no result directly establishing that the limit nef class arising from a unipotent automorphism of a Calabi–Yau threefold is induced by an invariant fibration. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Fibered Calabi-Yau threefolds with relative automorphisms of positive entropy and c_2-contractions
status_evidence.snippet: Structure theorems for fibered Calabi–Yau threefolds with positive-entropy automorphisms preserving the fibration.
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses fibrations preserved by automorphisms but does not resolve the unipotent limit-class question.

status_evidence.title: The classification of automorphisms and quotients of Calabi-Yau threefolds of type A
status_evidence.snippet: Classification results on Calabi–Yau threefold automorphisms.
status_evidence.claim: No statement here that the invariant nef limit class for a unipotent automorphism comes from a fibration.
